locality: Nabiac Pleistocene beach ridge barriers, 25 km south of Taree, lower north coast of NSW
description: Woodland with Eucalyptus racemosa subsp. racemosa dominant in the tree stratum, a well developed shrub stratum of Banksia aemula, Leptospermum trinervium and other species, and a ground stratum of small shrubs (Dillwynia retorta, Eriostemon australasius) and herbs (Caustis recurvata var. recurvata, Hypolaena fastigiata).
cemented_pan_depth_m: ~2.5-3 m thick pan at 3 m or more below the ridge surface
georeference_remarks: Coordinates are those given for the Nabiac barriers as a whole (32°09'S 152°26'E); the ridge site is ~3.2 km from the depression sites.
source_section: Study site and species; Results, Climate and groundwater depth; Discussion
notes: Soil type inferred from the catena description (Podzols on well-drained sites). MAP is the long-term mean for Taree. Shallow unconfined aquifer; watertable fluctuated 89 cm during water potential sampling.
